curriculum.lesson_evidence: A freeze frame, also called a still image, is a pose where actors hold still like a photograph to show a moment in a story. Choose a moment, decide who each person is, and show it with body shape, facial expression and the distance between people. Hold still for five seconds and breathe quietly. A thought bubble is when the leader taps a person and they say what their character is thinking. Be careful, and never touch or push others.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Plan a freeze frame of 'the winning goal' for a group of three. Say who each person is and what pose and face each would show.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'One player in a kicking pose with a proud face, one with both arms up cheering, one goalkeeper diving with a shocked face.' Different roles at different levels make the image clear, and each pose shows an emotion.

WATCH FOR
Believing that a freeze frame is just standing still and smiling. A good still image shows the moment and feelings through body shape and expression, and every person has a role.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Create three freeze frames for a story, such as the beginning, middle and end of a picnic. Draw or photograph each, write a thought bubble for one character in each and perform them for family. Stay safe and do not touch others.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: A freeze frame, also called a still image, is a pose where actors hold still like a photograph to show a moment in a story. Choose a moment, decide who each person is, and show it with body shape, facial expression and the distance between people. Hold still for five seconds and breathe quietly. A thought bubble is when the leader taps a person and they say what their character is thinking. Be careful, and never touch or push others. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
